lenovo-thinkpad-e14-gen-7-14-intel.display_max_resolution: 8K@60Hz (7680x4320) via Thunderbolt; HDMI up to 4096x2160@60Hz; USB-C up to 5120x2880@60Hz
lenovo-thinkpad-e14-gen-7-14-intel.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x1; USB-C (USB 20Gbps, DP 1.4) x1
lenovo-thinkpad-e14-gen-7-14-intel.display_detail: PSREF notes refresh rates above 60Hz are supported with reduced max resolution, and 8K output needs 2 display pipes so the simultaneous display count drops by 1; the second USB-C port appears as standard or optional depending on configuration.

lenovo-thinkpad-e16-gen-3-16-amd.display_max_resolution: 8K@60Hz (7680x4320) via USB4; HDMI and USB-C up to 4096x2160@60Hz
lenovo-thinkpad-e16-gen-3-16-amd.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C USB4 40Gbps (DP 1.4a) x1; USB-C 3.2 Gen 1 (DP 1.4) x1
lenovo-thinkpad-e16-gen-3-16-amd.display_detail: PSREF notes refresh rates above 60Hz are supported with reduced max resolution, and 8K output needs 2 display pipes so the simultaneous display count drops by 1.

lenovo-thinkpad-t14-gen-5-14-amd.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x2
lenovo-thinkpad-t14-gen-5-14-amd.display_detail: PSREF wording for the display path varies slightly by revision (HDMI plus Thunderbolt in later versions, HDMI plus USB-C in an earlier one); count and resolutions are consistent.

lenovo-thinkpad-t14-gen-5-14-intel.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x2
lenovo-thinkpad-t14-gen-5-14-intel.display_detail: PSREF notes refresh rates above 60Hz are supported with reduced max resolution, and 8K output needs 2 display pipes so the simultaneous display count drops by 1.

lenovo-thinkpad-x1-carbon-gen-13-aura-ed.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x2
lenovo-thinkpad-x1-carbon-gen-13-aura-ed.display_detail: PSREF splits this platform by CPU: V-series (Lunar Lake, e.g. Core Ultra 7 258V as sold in the Aura Edition) supports 2 external displays, while U/H-series (Arrow Lake) variants support 3; the value recorded is for the V-series Aura configuration.

lenovo-thinkpad-x13-2-in-1-gen-5-13-inte.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x2
lenovo-thinkpad-x13-2-in-1-gen-5-13-inte.display_detail: PSREF notes refresh rates above 60Hz are supported with reduced max resolution, and 8K output needs 2 display pipes so the simultaneous display count drops by 1.

lenovo-thinkpad-x13-gen-5-13-intel.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x2
lenovo-thinkpad-x13-gen-5-13-intel.display_detail: PSREF notes refresh rates above 60Hz are supported with reduced max resolution, and 8K output needs 2 display pipes so the simultaneous display count drops by 1.

lenovo-yoga-7i-2-in-1-gen-9-14-intel.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x2
lenovo-yoga-7i-2-in-1-gen-9-14-intel.display_detail: PSREF (Yoga 7 2-in-1 14IML9) notes 8K output needs 2 display pipes, so the simultaneous display count drops by 1 when driving 8K.

lenovo-yoga-9i-2-in-1-gen-10-aura-editio.display_ports: Thunderbolt 4 / USB4 (DP 2.1) x2; USB-C (USB4 Gen 2x2 20Gbps, DP 1.4) x1
lenovo-yoga-9i-2-in-1-gen-10-aura-editio.display_detail: PSREF per-model spec for Yoga 9 2-in-1 14ILL10 confirms the ports (no HDMI on this model), but no platform Monitor Support statement for 14ILL10 could be located in the Lenovo sources checked, so no display count or max resolution was recorded rather than inferred from the Lunar Lake platform.

lenovo-yoga-slim-7i-aura-edition-gen-10-.display_detail: PSREF (Yoga Slim 7 14ILL10) notes 8K output needs 2 display pipes, so the simultaneous display count drops by 1 when driving 8K.

lenovo-yoga-slim-7x-gen-9-14-snapdragon.display_detail: PSREF (Yoga Slim 7 14Q8X9) states all external displays run via USB-C; the model has no HDMI port, its only ports are 3x USB-C (USB4).

msi-katana-15-hx-b14w.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB-C (USB3.2 Gen2 / DisplayPort / Power Delivery 3.0) x1

microsoft-surface-laptop-13-8-inch-7th-e.display_detail: Microsoft Support table lists single (5120 x 2880 @ 60Hz) and dual (3840 x 2160 @ 60Hz) only, with the three-display column shown as '-' for Surface Laptop (7th Edition).

microsoft-surface-laptop-15-inch-7th-edi.display_detail: Microsoft Support uses one shared row for Surface Laptop (7th Edition) covering both sizes, listing single (5120 x 2880 @ 60Hz) and dual (3840 x 2160 @ 60Hz) only, with the three-display column shown as '-'; the 15-inch tech specs add a microSDXC reader but the same 2x USB-C/USB4 display ports.

microsoft-surface-laptop-studio-2.display_detail: Microsoft Support table for Surface Laptop Studio lists only single and dual columns for Studio 2: single 5120 x 3200 @ 120Hz, dual 4096 x 2304 @ 60Hz, with no three-display column.

microsoft-surface-laptop-for-business-13.display_ports: USB-C with USB4 / Thunderbolt 4 x2 (DisplayPort 2.1 on Intel variant)
microsoft-surface-laptop-for-business-13.display_detail: Both variants support three displays per Microsoft: Support table lists Snapdragon (8th Edition) and Intel for Business (8th Edition) rows identically (single 5120 x 2880 @ 60Hz, dual and three 3840 x 2160 @ 60Hz), and the Intel Business tech specs state DisplayPort 2.1 support for up to three 4K mo

razer-blade-14.display_detail: Razer lists ports only on its product page (dual USB4 Type-C, full-size HDMI 2.1) and states no external-display count; the page notes the USB4 ports can link to a Thunderbolt dock/hub.

razer-blade-16-2026.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 FRL x1; Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) x1; Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) x1
razer-blade-16-2026.display_detail: Razer tech specs list the HDMI and both Thunderbolt ports as supporting DisplayPort/power delivery, but Razer states no external-display count for this model.

razer-blade-18.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) x1; Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) x1 (listed as USB-C on the product page)
razer-blade-18.display_detail: Razer's Blade 18 pages list Thunderbolt 5, Thunderbolt 4/USB-C and HDMI 2.1 ports and an HDMI cap of 4K at 144Hz, but state no external-display count for this model.

samsung-galaxy-book4-edge.display_detail: Samsung lists the same HDMI 2.1 (Supports 4K@60Hz) spec for the X1E-80-100 14-inch model checked and the 16-inch model; no different display support per X1E-80 vs X1E-84 chip was stated on the Samsung pages checked.

samsung-galaxy-book4-edge-15.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; USB 4.0 x2; USB 3.2 x1
samsung-galaxy-book4-edge-15.display_detail: Samsung spec for the 15.6-inch X1-26-100 model states HDMI 2.1 (Supports 4K@60Hz); the US page also lists the 15-inch model with Snapdragon X / X Plus and HDMI 2.1 / USB 4.0 ports.

samsung-galaxy-book5.display_ports: HDMI x1; USB Type-C x2; USB 3.2 x2
samsung-galaxy-book5.display_detail: Samsung lists HDMI with no version or external resolution/refresh stated for this Core Ultra 7 255U model.
samsung-galaxy-book5.unknown_reason: Samsung's spec pages for the Galaxy Book5 (NP750XHD) list "2 x USB Type-C" with no DisplayPort, alt-mode, or Thunderbolt statement anywhere in Samsung's published specifications for the model. Retailer copy implies more than Samsung states; per policy the class is not guessed.

samsung-galaxy-book5-360.display_ports: HDMI x1; Thunderbolt 4 x2; USB 3.2 x1
samsung-galaxy-book5-360.display_detail: Samsung lists HDMI with no version or external resolution/refresh stated, unlike the Book5 Pro models which state HDMI 2.1 with 8K@60Hz / 5K@120Hz; Samsung newsroom port list for Book5 360 likewise gives HDMI without a resolution.

samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-14.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; Thunderbolt 4 x2; USB 3.2 x1
samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-14.display_detail: Samsung states the HDMI port as '1 HDMI 2.1 (Supports 8K@60Hz, 5K@120Hz)'.

samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-16.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; Thunderbolt 4 x2; USB 3.2 x1
samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-16.display_detail: Samsung states the HDMI port as '1 HDMI 2.1 (Supports 8K@60Hz, 5K@120Hz)'.

samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-360.display_ports: HDMI 2.1 x1; Thunderbolt 4 x2; USB 3.2 x1
samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-360.display_detail: Samsung states the HDMI port as '1 HDMI 2.1 (Supports 8K@60Hz, 5K@120Hz)'.

samsung-galaxy-chromebook-plus.display_ports: HDMI 1.4 x1; USB Type-C x2; USB 3.2 x1
samsung-galaxy-chromebook-plus.display_detail: Samsung (governing source) lists '1 HDMI 1.4' and 2 USB Type-C with no external resolution, refresh, or USB-C display-output statement; no platform-source fallback was used because Samsung was not silent on ports, only on external resolution/count.

1080p.name: BenQ GW2490
1080p.why: The everyday value pick: 100Hz IPS with two HDMI ports plus DisplayPort, built-in speakers and BenQ eye-care modes, at the lowest price on this shelf.

1080p.name: Dell P2425H
1080p.why: The office all-rounder: height, swivel and pivot stand, 99% sRGB IPS at 100Hz and a real USB hub - just do not expect its USB-C port to carry video.

1080p.name: BenQ GW2486TC
1080p.why: The laptop pick: one USB-C cable carries video, data and 65W charging, and you still get a height-adjustable stand, speakers, a noise-cancelling mic and a USB hub.

1080p.name: Samsung Odyssey G3 G30D (LS24DG302ENXZA)
1080p.why: The gaming pick: a true native 180Hz with FreeSync and a height-adjustable stand, on a VA panel with deep 3,000:1 contrast for dark scenes.

1080p.name: Deco Gear 49-inch Curved Ultrawide - DGVIEW490
1080p.why: Two 27-inch 1080p screens fused into one 49-inch curved panel, with one-cable USB-C video (65W charging), a built-in KVM, and 144Hz - the budget way to replace a two-monitor desk with a single screen.

1440p.name: Dell 27 Gaming Monitor - G2724D
1440p.why: Cheapest honest 1440p IPS here: 400-nit Fast IPS at 165Hz with a full height/pivot stand and VESA mount, as long as you do not need USB or speakers.

1440p.name: ASUS TUF Gaming VG27AQ3A
1440p.why: Fastest panel on the shelf at 180Hz with built-in 2W x2 speakers for $209, if you can live with a dim 250-nit screen and no height adjustment.

1440p.name: LG UltraGear 27GR75Q-B
1440p.why: Balanced middle pick: factory color-calibrated 165Hz IPS with a height/pivot stand, fine for work by day and games by night.

1440p.name: Dell UltraSharp 27 Monitor - U2724D
1440p.why: Best color on the shelf for the money: IPS Black panel, 100% sRGB and 98% DCI-P3 with a stated Delta E < 2 average, at 120Hz, if your computer connects by HDMI or DisplayPort.

1440p.name: Dell UltraSharp 27 Thunderbolt Hub Monitor - U2724DE
1440p.role: creator-leaning / work docking pick (single-cable laptop pick)
1440p.why: The one-cable desk pick: same calibrated IPS Black 1440p 120Hz panel as the U2724D, plus a real Thunderbolt dock with 90W charging, KVM and 2.5GbE Ethernet built in.

1440p.name: Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G93SD) - LS49DG934SNXGO
1440p.why: Two 27-inch QHD screens fused into one 49-inch QD-OLED with no center bezel: 240Hz, 0.03ms and 99% DCI-P3 for racing, flight sims and sprawling timelines.

1440p.name: ASUS ProArt Display PA34VCNV
1440p.why: The creator ultrawide value pick: factory-calibrated IPS with Delta E < 2, 100% sRGB and Rec.709, a 96W USB-C dock with Ethernet and daisy-chaining, at a mid-range price.

1440p.name: MSI MPG 491CQP QD-OLED
1440p.why: A 49-inch QD-OLED super-ultrawide - about three monitors of desk - with true blacks, 144Hz, and one-cable USB-C video with 90W charging, for $200 less than Samsung's OLED G9.

1440p.name: Lenovo ThinkVision P49w-30
1440p.why: A 49-inch IPS Black super-ultrawide built as a full docking station: Thunderbolt 4 with 100W charging, Ethernet, eKVM, and a Thunderbolt output to daisy-chain a second screen. Caleb found the US listing the morning sweep had to give up on.

1440p.name: CRUA CR490QW 49-inch Curved Ultrawide
1440p.why: A 49-inch 5120x1440 curved VA panel at 240Hz for $699.99 direct from the maker - the fastest super-ultrawide on the shelf for the money. HDMI/DisplayPort only; there is no USB-C.

1440p.name: Alienware AW2726DM 27-inch QD-OLED
1440p.why: The cheapest way into OLED gaming: a 1440p QD-OLED at 240Hz for $349.99 - Dell got there by cutting the USB hub, speakers and brightness, not the panel.

1440p.name: LG UltraGear 27GX790A-B
1440p.why: The speed king: 480Hz on a 26.5-inch WOLED with DisplayPort 2.1 and True Black 400 - the fastest monitor on this shelf, built purely for competitive play.

1440p.name: Alienware AW3425DW 34-inch Curved QD-OLED Ultrawide
1440p.why: The ultrawide OLED sweet spot: 34.2 inches of 3440x1440 QD-OLED at 240Hz with 99.3% DCI-P3 and true blacks - just bring your own speakers, and don't expect the USB-C port to carry video.

4k.name: Dell 27 Plus 4K USB-C Monitor - S2725QC
4k.why: True 4K at 120Hz with 99% sRGB, speakers and a 65W single-cable USB-C dock for the lowest price on the shelf.

4k.name: Samsung ViewFinity S8 S80UD 27-inch - LS27D802UANXGO
4k.why: True 4K IPS with 99% sRGB, HDR10, KVM, Ethernet and the strongest laptop charging on the shelf at 90W over USB-C.

4k.name: ASUS ProArt Display PA279CV
4k.why: Factory-calibrated 100% sRGB, Delta E < 2, Calman Verified, with USB-C 65W video and a 4-port USB hub for under $400.

4k.name: BenQ PD2705U
4k.why: Designer monitor with 99% sRGB / 99% Rec.709, factory calibration report, Calman and Pantone validation, KVM and 65W USB-C video in one cable.

4k.name: Dell UltraSharp 43 4K USB-C Hub Monitor - U4323QE
4k.why: A 42.5-inch 4K IPS screen that is also the dock: real USB-C video with 90W charging, KVM, Ethernet and built-in speakers, so one big panel can replace a dual-monitor setup.

4k.name: Dell UltraSharp 40 Curved Thunderbolt Hub Monitor - U4025QW
4k.why: The widescreen dock flagship: 5K2K IPS Black at 120Hz with 99% DCI-P3, DisplayHDR 600, Thunderbolt 4 with up to 140W charging, KVM and 2.5GbE Ethernet in one curved 40-inch panel.

4k.name: LG UltraGear 45GX950A-B
4k.why: The biggest OLED canvas here: a 45-inch-class 5K2K panel at 165Hz (or 330Hz in Dual Mode) with DisplayHDR True Black 400 and 98.5% DCI-P3 - a sim cockpit and a giant editing desk in one.

4k.name: LG UltraGear evo 52G930B-B
4k.why: A 52-inch 5K2K curved ultrawide - roughly two monitors wide in a single panel - with 240Hz, DisplayHDR 600, and one-cable USB-C video with 90W charging.

4k.name: Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 57-inch - LS57CG952NNXZA
4k.why: Two 32-inch 4K screens fused into one 57-inch Mini-LED panel - about three monitors of desk - with 240Hz and DisplayHDR 1000. No USB-C: it pairs over HDMI or DisplayPort.

4k.name: Samsung ViewFinity S8 37-inch (S80UD) - LS37D800UANXZA
4k.why: A 37-inch 4K panel - Large class without the 43-inch price - with a built-in dock: USB-C 90W charging, Ethernet, and a KVM switch, so one cable runs a laptop's screen, network, and peripherals.

4k.name: LG 37U730SA-W Smart Monitor
4k.why: A 37-inch 4K IPS panel - Large class - that is also a webOS smart TV: streaming apps with no computer attached, plus one-cable USB-C (65W) for a laptop. Caleb found this one on LG's store.

4k.name: Alienware AW2725Q 27-inch 4K QD-OLED
4k.why: The sharpest gaming monitor on this shelf: full 4K on a 26.7-inch QD-OLED (165 PPI) at 240Hz with Dolby Vision - desktop-class text clarity that still plays at esports speed.

4k.name: Alienware AW3225QF 32-inch 4K QD-OLED
4k.why: The big-screen 4K OLED: a gently curved 31.6-inch QD-OLED at 240Hz with 99% DCI-P3 and Dolby Vision, for gamers who want near-TV size without giving up monitor speed.

4k.name: HP OMEN Transcend 32
4k.role: gaming-leaning / work docking pick (4K OLED with full USB-C)
4k.why: The one-cable OLED: the only OLED on this shelf whose USB-C takes video AND delivers 140W, with a KVM switch, DisplayPort 2.1 and built-in speakers - a gaming flagship that also docks a laptop, at a clearance price half its $1,299.99 list.
